Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

sdvplotR 0.1.0

Initial release: team logos, wordmarks, player headshots and team colours for ggplot2, gt and reactable, and for interactive plotly, ggiraph and leaflet charts, across the 28 leagues of the SportsDataverse team index (sdv_leagues()), built on ‘ggpath’. It shares its team index, logo archive and argument names with the Python package sdvplot and the JavaScript packages @sportsdataverse/sdvplot and @sportsdataverse/sdvtables.

Teams and identifiers

  • sdv_resolve() turns team identifiers from any of 19 id systems (ESPN, nflverse, MLB Stats, nba_api, NHL, HockeyTech, CFBD, NCAA, PFF, Sports Reference, FanGraphs, names, …) into canonical team ids, using season for codes reused across eras; sdv_suggest() proposes candidates for a value that does not resolve. The helpers that take a team take league and id_system. Those that draw team marks or colours also take season (the geom_sdv_* layers read it as an aesthetic or a constant). strict (raise instead of warn when a value does not resolve) is taken by sdv_resolve(), sdv_logo_url(), sdv_team_colors(), sdv_color_palette(), sdv_team_tiers() and the logo, wordmark, label and colour-bar helpers (geom_sdv_logos(), geom_sdv_wordmarks(), add_sdv_logos(), add_sdv_wordmarks(), addSdvLogoMarkers(), sdv_axis_logos() and the gt_sdv_* and reactable_sdv_* helpers that draw them), but not by sdv_marks(), element_sdv_logo(), element_sdv_wordmark(), scale_x_sdv(), scale_y_sdv(), sdv_colorway() or sdv_team_factor(). Headshot helpers take no season; ggtitle_image(), scale_colour_sdv(), scale_color_sdv() and scale_fill_sdv() take neither season nor id_system; sdv_surface() takes league and season but no id_system.
  • sdv_teams(), sdv_leagues(), sdv_team_colors(), sdv_color_palette() and sdv_team_factor() list and colour teams.
  • The team index and the logo manifest are read from the SportsDataverse CDN and cached for a day (sdv_versions(), sdv_clear_cache()); a copy is bundled for offline use (options(sdvplotR.offline = TRUE)).

Logos, wordmarks and headshots

  • sdv_logo_url() and sdv_marks() choose a team’s archived mark by variant ("default", "dark", or a named variant) and season.
  • sdv_headshot_url() and the headshot helpers read ESPN athlete ids in every league by default; id_system = "gsis" reads nflverse NFL ids and id_system = "league" the league’s own player ids.

Interactive plots and maps

  • plotly: add_sdv_logos(), add_sdv_wordmarks(), add_sdv_headshots(), sdv_axis_logos() and sdv_colorway().
  • ggiraph: geom_sdv_logos_interactive(), geom_sdv_wordmarks_interactive() and geom_sdv_headshots_interactive(), which embed images at most max_px
    1. pixels a side, so 32 logos add about half a megabyte to the page.
  • leaflet: addSdvLogoMarkers().

Plots, surfaces and tables

  • geom_sdv_logos(), geom_sdv_wordmarks() and geom_sdv_headshots() draw images at x / y positions; geom_sdv_logos() takes a season aesthetic, so a team is drawn with the mark it wore that season.
  • element_sdv_logo(), element_sdv_wordmark() and element_sdv_headshot() replace axis text with images; scale_x_sdv(), scale_y_sdv() and the headshot variants do the same through ggtext::element_markdown() with theme_x_sdv() / theme_y_sdv(). Both draw a copy of each image at most four times its drawn size (sharp in a 300 dpi export, and a few KB a logo in an SVG or ggiraph widget). All of them work after a complete theme such as theme_minimal() on ‘ggplot2’ 4, which sdvplotR requires.
  • gt_theme_source() and reactable_sdv_theme() apply any of 122 surveyed table styles, named for their source ("datagolf", "wikipedia", "nejm", …); sdv_table_themes() lists them and table_theme_spec() resolves one. The registry is shared with sdvplot and sdvtables. Twenty shortcuts such as gt_theme_datagolf() and gt_theme_wikipedia() name the most useful.
  • scale_color_sdv() and scale_fill_sdv() map teams to their primary or secondary colours.
  • Conference rows (the college conferences, and the AFC, NFC and NFL) have logos and colours: sdv_teams(include_conferences = TRUE) lists them and the image helpers draw them from their short keys ("SEC", "Big Ten", "Pac-12") or their other names ("Southeastern Conference", "B1G"). A team’s code wins over a conference’s: cfb’s "MAC" is Macalester.
  • sdv_team_tiers() builds tier charts, with dark marks on its dark theme (variant = "auto") and a theme = "light" option; ggtitle_image() with theme_title_image() places a logo next to a plot title.
  • sdv_surface() draws a court, field, rink, pitch or sheet through ‘sportyR’ for 59 surface keys, the table sdvplot (Python) and sdvplot-js share, as a ggplot to plot data on: every sport ‘sportyR’ draws (basketball, football, baseball, softball, hockey, soccer, lacrosse, tennis, volleyball, curling) and its leagues, from the NFL to NFHS, Little League, the ATP and the WCF. Leagues without a surface of their own use their sport’s (the WHL, for one, uses the NHL rink); the PWHL draws its own rink. Given a team, a few features take its colours, and center_logo = TRUE puts its logo at the center; on a baseball or softball field, whose origin is home plate, it goes in shallow center field instead, midway between second base and the center-field fence and 0.15 x the center-field distance across (it used to warn and draw no logo), as in sdvplot (Python). These are stylized surfaces built from team colours, not the teams’ real floor, field or rink designs. Keys that are not team leagues ("fiba", "atp", "nll", "epl", …) take no team. "ncaa_softball" is both a team league and a surface and needs ‘sportyR’ 2.3.0, not yet on CRAN; with an older ‘sportyR’ it errors naming the version and remotes::install_github("sportsdataverse/sportyR").
  • sdv_court_coords() converts stats.nba.com / stats.wnba.com legacy shot locations (x_legacy/y_legacy, or LOC_X/LOC_Y from the Shot_Chart_Detail element of hoopR::nba_shotchartdetail()) into the sportyR::geom_basketball("nba") court frame; the converted points also fit sportyR’s "wnba" and "ncaa" courts. sdv_court_coords(provider = "euroleague") converts the Euroleague shot frame of hoopR’s euroleague_game_points() (coord_x/coord_y: integer centimeters, hoop at the origin, both teams on one basket, free throws as -1,-1) onto the FIBA court sdv_surface("fiba") draws, in meters, with the -1,-1 free throws as NA.
  • sdv_pitch_coords() converts soccer event coordinates from Opta / Stats Perform, Wyscout, StatsBomb, UEFA, Impect, ESPN and the tracking providers (Tracab, SkillCorner, Second Spectrum, Metrica) to one regulation 105 x 68 m frame, piecewise-linearly between pitch landmarks.
  • gt_sdv_logos(), gt_sdv_wordmarks(), gt_sdv_headshots(), gt_sdv_cols_label() and gt_merge_stack_team_color() render images and team-coloured text inside ‘gt’ tables. gt_sdv_logos(include_name = TRUE) keeps the cell’s text after the logo. gt_merge_stack_team_color() keeps its text readable: a primary colour under 4.5:1 contrast against the cell background gives way to the secondary colour, or is darkened until it passes.
  • reactable_sdv_logos(), reactable_sdv_wordmarks(), reactable_sdv_headshots(), reactable_sdv_cols_label(), reactable_sdv_team_color_bar() and reactable_sdv_team_color_bg() do the same for ‘reactable’ tables; a logo or wordmark swaps to the default image in the browser if a variant fails to load.
  • gt_theme_sdv() is the SportsDataverse house table theme, in light and style = "dark", and gt_theme_sdv_team() dresses a table in one team’s colours from sdv_team_colors(), picking title text and line colours by contrast.
  • The ‘gtUtils’ table toolkit by Andrew Weatherman ships in sdvplotR: 18 gt_theme_*() table themes plus gt_theme_preview(), continuous and discrete colour legends, gt_cutline(), gt_significance(), gt_outliers(), colour pills / ranks / results, percentile bars, border bars, gt_grid(), gt_snake() and gt_stack_tables() layouts, gt_save_crop(), gt_save_batch() and gt_social_crop(), and the theme_bg background lookup. The eight gtUtils articles are on the website as “gt Table Cookbooks”.
  • Every gt_theme_*() keeps its own row colours on a Bootstrap page (pkgdown, Quarto) in either colour mode. gt_color_pills(), gt_percentile_bar(), gt_fmt_tally(), gt_significance() and gt_merge_stack_team_color() decorate each cell from its own row when row groups reorder the table. gt_grid() and gt_stack_tables() scroll inside their own box when they are wider than the screen.
  • gt_spotlight() dims the other rows to a readable tone: with dim_color = "auto" it blends the table’s text toward its background until it sits just above 4.5:1 contrast. gt_tiers() gives each image its own alt text, and takes an alt argument for your own text.
  • Saving a table to an image (gt_save_crop(), gt_social_crop(), gt_save_batch(), gt_grid(), gt_stack_tables()) gives headless Chrome 60 seconds to start; a longer options(chromote.timeout = ) of your own is kept. gt_save_batch() needs an explicit dir.
  • Every example runs: examples that only build tables run as plain examples, and those that save images through a headless Chrome are \donttest{} blocks that run in an interactive session with webshot2 and Chrome available. The reference examples use real SportsDataverse data: sdv_example_standings holds the final 2025 NFL and 2025-26 NBA regular-season standings, built by data-raw/sdv_examples.R from the nflreadr / nflseedR and hoopR release loaders.
  • The package ships no vignettes. Every article, “Getting Started” included, is on the pkgdown site (https://sdvplotR.sportsdataverse.org/articles/), among them “SportsDataverse Table Themes”, “Team Tables with the gt Toolkit” and a “Visual recipes” group that rebuilds SportsDataverse web visuals as static tables and plots on real data.
